exposure: Cesarean delivery during the second stage of labor
cohort: The study included women who experienced urinary tract injury during cesarean delivery at a tertiary medical center between 2004 and 2018.
finding: Urinary tract injuries are uncommon complications of cesarean delivery (bladder injury incidence 0.08%, ureteral injury incidence 0.06%), and none of the affected patients suffered long-term adverse effects or sequelae.
mod_finding: Bladder injuries were predominantly observed in women with previous cesarean delivery and abdominal adhesions, whereas ureteral injuries were mostly associated with emergency cesarean delivery during the second stage of labor and uterine incision extensions.
followup_time: Long-term (specific duration not mentioned, but included telephone interviews for long-term outcomes)
